messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — did a perf pass on main + kv-memoization. Seeing ~22% TPS regression for FP8 prefill on 64k longctx when hybrid4bit kernel selection is enabled. Repro steps below.

alex: repro:
```
./run_bench --model gemma-13b --quant fp8 --kernel-select hybrid4bit --kv-mode memoize --context 65536 --batch 8 --warm 5 --iters 100
```

alex: summary (avg over 3 runs):
```
Mode             | Prefill TPS | Decode TPS | Prefill TTFT
FP32 baseline     |  70.3       |  120.1     | 85ms
FP8 + hybrid4bit  |  54.9       |  115.4     | 98ms
INT8              |  66.2       |  116.7     | 88ms
4bit              |  61.8       |  110.3     | 92ms
```

alex: note prefill TPS drop is bigger than TTFT increase; looks like batching/kernel switch overhead during prefill path when kv cache writes happen.

maria: interesting. Can you capture per-layer kernel selection timeline? suspect we're reloading quant/dequant kernels per-layer at prefill time. Also check per-layer scale calibration fallback (we saw the Mar 3 change that toggled per-layer fallback on large layers).

alex: attached timeline (snippet):
```
[00:00.123] layer 1: choose kernel fp8_matmul_hybrid4
[00:00.130] layer 1: quant_dequant init (cuda memcpy)
[00:00.210] layer 2: choose kernel fp8_matmul_hybrid4
[00:00.218] layer 2: kv_cache write
[00:00.350] layer N: kernel switch overhead + sync
```

sam: can you bisect the kernel selection change? I think the scheduler started toggling kernels based on sequence-length percentile on Mar 3 (commit 6a2b). If it's toggling per-layer during prefill it's expensive. Maybe lock kernel per-prefill-request to avoid per-layer re-eval.

maria: Also try forcing `--kernel-policy=static` vs `adaptive` to compare.

alex: ran quick A/B with kernel-policy static:
```
static: prefill TPS 68.0
adaptive: prefill TPS 55.1
```

alex: so adaptive policy is the culprit when memoization + longctx prefill present. Hypothesis: adaptive probes extra kernels (fallbacks) which trigger GPU syncs and mallocs on the prefill path.

perf-bot: perf-run 1934567890 attached. Regression detected: prefill_tps down -21.5% relative to baseline on longctx/fp8 with adaptive-kernel & memoize. Added perf trace to https://perf.redwood/trace/1934567890

maria: mitigation plan: 1) short-term: disable adaptive probing during prefill (only allow static selection), 2) medium: amortize kernel init by pre-allocating scratch and doing async kernel warmup, 3) long-term: move kernel probe off hot path and record confident selection in model profile cache.

sam: agree. I'll open a PR to gate adaptive probing behind `allow_probe_on_prefill=false` defaulting to false for longctx > 32k. assign @alex to test.

alex: noted. I'll run a smoke matrix across fp8/int8/4bit + memoize with static policy and post numbers.

maria: also add a calibration check: if per-layer `scale_fallback=true` is logged, it forces extra dequant which may block prefill. If you see that, treat as red flag.

alex: got it, will grep logs for `scale_fallback` and `kernel_probe` events and upload traces.

sam: thanks. Monday sync: ship quick patch to avoid adaptive probing on prefill; follow-up perf run after patch.

alex: :thumbsup:
